newsitem.title: USA: Texas jury awards $5.5 million in TV libel suit.
newsitem.headline: Texas jury awards $5.5 million in TV libel suit.

text.p: A Texas jury on Monday awarded an unsuccessful Houston mayoral candidate $5.5 million in damages for a 1991 television report that he blamed for his election loss.

The jury found that a report by KTRK-TV in Houston had defamed Sylvester Turner, now a member of the Texas legislature, when it linked him to an alleged 1986 insurance scam in which a former client had faked his own death.
The story came out shortly before a hotly-contested mayoral race that Turner lost to Mayor Bob Lanier. Turner said the report was untrue and that it turned a tide that had been running in his favor.
"I simply felt from the beginning, and the jurors confirmed today, that the story was defamatory, that the story was false, that the story was run with malice," Turner said after the verdict.

The jury, which deliberated for a week after listening to a month of testimony, said reporter Wayne Dolcefino must pay $500,000 of the $5.5 million in damages, with the station responsible for the rest.
Dolcefino had no comment, but KTRK-TV, which is owned by ABC Inc., a unit of Walt Disney Co., said in a statement that it was "extremely disappointed" with the verdict.
"We believe that the outcome was wrong and plan to vigorously pursue an appeal," the statement said.
